rationale: A wins by a nose because it gives four genuinely usable newsroom lanes, and "Patagonia is building reverse logistics for clothing at national scale" is the kind of operations angle a trade reporter can actually report. B is disciplined and useful, especially "Without at least the time period, this angle is a bare number and should not be pitched," but it lets "nobody else can copy the math" run miles past the evidence. The win is not about more angles; it is about A having one extra real retail-economics lane without quite as much unsupported swagger.
gaps_in_A: "Only a company with no shareholders to please could give repairs away" overstates the supplied fact. The update says privately held and directs profits to environmental causes; it does not prove no shareholder pressure or that only Patagonia can do this.

"a network that takes any item of the brand, in any store or by mail, triages it into free/at-cost/resale" invents an operational link between repair intake and resale routing. The update does not say repaired items are routed into Worn Wear resale.
"repairs are a cost center retailers minimize" may be true, but it is unsupported background in this packet. The angle needs repair-volume or cost data before that economics claim can carry a pitch.
The next step jumps to `journalist-fit-check` too soon. The sharper move is to verify whether this is genuinely new or already well covered before burning reporter names.
gaps_in_B: "nobody else can copy the math" is the worst sentence in either set. There is no repair-cost math, no peer comparison, and no evidence that public apparel companies cannot copy the model.
"category-creation" inflates a repair-program expansion. The facts support a retail-operations or reverse-logistics story, not a new category unless peers, adoption, and market context are proven.
"Patagonia will now fix your jacket" narrows "any Patagonia item" into jacket shorthand and makes the operations angle read more like consumer-service copy.
B loses the cleaner standalone contrarian retail-economics angle. Its ownership angle tries to carry both capital structure and business-model tension, then buckles under the unsupported headline.
